newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler seeks to cool EU-U.S. grain tension.
newsitem.headline: Fischler seeks to cool EU-U.S. grain tension.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler tried on Tuesday to cool growing transatlantic tensions over grain export subsidies, saying EU refunds were based on U.S. prices.
Fischler said he had replied to a recent letter from U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman about the resumption of wheat export subsidies.
"I made it clear to him that we are calculating subsidies on the basis of U.S. prices in Chicago," Fischler told Reuters, after addressing the Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS).
But Fischler sidestepped a question on whether a massive EU grain crop and falling world prices would bring increasing EU export subsidies and an escalation of trade tension with the U.S.
On Friday in Washington, Glickman issued a new warning to the EU that he would fight subsidies with subsidies.
The EU earlier this month restarted wheat export subsidies, after a gap of more than a year, as world prices fell below EU levels.
